description.value: 25 racial Hit Dice, d8, three-quarter base attack, good Will. The 113 hit points here are the dice before Constitution and Toughness.
Living parasitic aberration. The voremind subtype marks the same species. Not undead.

The Voremind

The Voremind are not creatures of death. They are life stripped of individuality, a biological consciousness that views all living things as incomplete pieces of itself.

Unlike the undead, the Voremind do not raise corpses through necromancy. They consume and reconstruct organic material, weaving living tissue into entirely new organisms.

Their most terrifying trait is that they keep the memories of the creatures they assimilate. As their numbers grow, so does their collective intelligence.

Ancient scholars of the Grand Archive called the outbreak the Carrion Bloom. They believed they were containing a disease. What they actually imprisoned was an intelligent species.

Every Voremind creature is a living aberration, not undead. Positive energy heals it. Negative energy harms it. Undead-only effects, including channel energy against undead, do not treat it as undead. It is immune to Assimilating Blight and not immune to other diseases. It can be critically hit, sneaked, poisoned, and affected by mind-affecting effects unless a statblock says otherwise.

Assimilating Blight is an extraordinary biological disease. Injury or inhaled, as the attack says. Onset 1 round, frequency 1/round for 6 rounds, 1d2 Constitution and 1d2 Wisdom damage, sickened for 1 round on a failed save, cure 2 consecutive saves. A creature that dies infected, or whose Constitution or Wisdom reaches 0 from the disease, becomes one of the Reclaimed after 1d4 rounds if the body is intact. Remove disease or heal ends the blight before that change. After the change, the creature is a new aberration.

It speaks to every Voremind within 10 miles. Allied Voremind within 1 mile gain +2 insight on attack rolls and saving throws. Once a round, as a swift action, it can give one Voremind within 1 mile an extra move action on that creature's next turn.

Crushing mind pulse. Once every 1d4 rounds, 120-foot-radius burst, 15d6 untyped psychic damage to living enemies, Will DC 31 half, and confused for 1d4 rounds on a failure. Mind-affecting.

Distributed consciousness. +4 racial bonus on saves against mind-affecting effects. It is not immune. Destroying this body destroys this statblock. An established colony can keep copies of the memories.

Constrict. 3d8+18. Assimilating Blight from the tentacles, Fortitude DC 33.

Harvested Consciousness. When an infected creature dies within 120 feet, the Thousandfold Mind may take its memories and gain 10 temporary hit points, to a maximum of 100, lasting 1 hour.

Spell-like abilities. Caster level 20, concentration +27. At will: detect thoughts (DC 19), greater scrying (DC 24), suggestion (DC 20), telekinesis (DC 22). 3/day: dominate monster (DC 26), mass suggestion (DC 23), mind fog (DC 22). 1/day: mass hold monster (DC 26), telepathic bond (Voremind only). Psychic mastery lets it use the quickened suggestion as a swift action, up to three times a day, without a second action.

Living Reconstruction. Fast healing 20, suppressed until the end of its next turn after fire or acid.

This is a contained node. It is not the whole Voremind.
Reach 30 feet. Grab. Improved Critical makes the threat range 19–20. Constrict 3d8+18. Assimilating Blight Fortitude DC 33.
Once every 1d4 rounds. Living enemies in a 120-foot burst. Mind-affecting. No energy type.

A local node of the Voremind's mind, not the whole consciousness. A hill of flesh, tentacles, and stolen thought. It is the oldest surviving intelligence of the Voremind, and it remembers every attempt to destroy it.

The Thousandfold Mind — CR 18, XP 153,600.

Conduct

It does not fight alone. The lesser Voremind are the weapon. It uses what it learned from people who are already dead, and it leaves a copy of itself in the colony if this body is destroyed.
